what: U.S. Bancorp is one of the largest regional banks in the United States. It does retail and commercial banking across the Midwest and West, and runs one of the country's biggest payment processing businesses for merchants and card issuers.
customers: Households and businesses in its branch footprint, corporate clients nationally, and merchants and banks using its payments services.
money: Wholesale Banking and Commercial Real Estate
merchant acquiring, corporate cards and card issuing
moat: A payments business that earns fees from transactions rather than lending, which few regional banks have, alongside a long-standing deposit base.
risks: Payments faces competition from technology-led processors
Commercial property lending is watched across all regional banks
Deposit costs rise as customers move to higher-yielding accounts
Regional bank capital rules are being tightened
opportunities: Payment fees grow with card spending and do not consume capital
Cost discipline after the Union Bank integration is lifting efficiency
A dividend yield above 3.5% with a long increase record
watch: Payment services revenue growth and net interest margin.
